Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for taking our call earlier — AcmeAssist is evaluating the Voice Assist feature for a pilot and our privacy/compliance team has a short SSQ related to PII handling. Two specific asks to start:

1) Can you share a detailed dataflow diagram for the transcription pipeline (ingest -> transcription model -> storage -> telemetry/export)? We need to show which components see raw audio/transcripts and any points where data is pseudonymized or redacted.

2) For PII in transcripts, what are your recommended modes: pre-ingest redaction, tokenization, or post-process pseudonymization? Please indicate what is default for Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private.

Other items we will ask later: retention windows for raw audio vs derived text, BYO-KMS support, and subprocessor mapping by region (we need to know which subprocessors could access EU data).

Attached is our SSQ template — if you can answer inline and attach a diagram that would be ideal. We are aiming for a compliance review next week and would like any clarifications in writing.

Hi Elda,

Thanks — appreciate the clear asks. I've answered the two items inline below and attached a labeled dataflow diagram and a compact SSQ answer matrix for your records. Short summary up-front: default Hosted is minimal redaction + short-lived KV caching, Dedicated supports stronger pre-ingest redaction and optional BYO-KMS, and Private (VPC/on-prem) supports full BYO-KMS and customer-controlled key custody.

--- Answers (high-level) ---
1) Dataflow diagram: attached (redwood_voiceassist_dataflow_v2.pdf).
   - Ingest: audio arrives via TLS to the edge. If configured, an optional pre-ingest redaction filter runs to remove PII (regex/ML redactor).
   - Transcoding: audio is normalized and chunked by TranscodeCloud (subprocessor). Raw audio is not persisted beyond transient storage unless customer enables recording retention.
   - Transcription model: audio -> model in the serving runtime. The runtime keeps a minimal in-memory KV cache (ephemeral) by default (TTL 24h) for prompt/context; KV persistence is configurable per deployment.
   - Post-process: transcript can be routed through tokenization/pseudonymization (we call this the "PII scrubber" step) before long-term storage.
   - Storage: final transcripts and debug logs are written to the blobstore. Telemetry and metrics are forwarded to MetricsStack (subprocessor) with PII-stripping applied.

2) Recommended modes (default vs options):
   - Hosted API (default): minimal on-the-fly redaction + ephemeral KV cache (24h). By default we do not persist raw audio; transcripts are stored unless customer opts out. PII scrubber is available as an opt-in pipeline stage.
   - Dedicated: supports enforced pre-ingest redaction at the edge and configurable retention; can enable stronger tokenization before storage.
   - Private (VPC / on-prem): full customer control: BYO-KMS, no Redwood-managed long-term raw audio storage unless customer allows.

Subprocessors (short list): TranscodeCloud (audio normalization/transcoding), StorageTier (blobstore), MetricsStack (telemetry/metrics), ThirdEye (monitoring/alerting). Full subprocessor roster and regional mapping in the attached SSQ matrix.

BYO-KMS: Supported for Private deployments. For Dedicated we support HSM-backed keys via our sig-int integration (we can scope a key-custody design for the contract). Hosted can integrate with customer KMS in limited scenarios for encryption-at-rest of customer blobs; we should discuss scope.

Retention defaults and logs: default raw-audio retention = 0 days (not persisted) unless explicitly enabled. Transcript retention default = 30 days; we have configurable retention policy tiers (30/90/365/custom). Audit logs and exported evidence can be generated via the Console.

Attachments: redwood_voiceassist_dataflow_v2.pdf (diagram), ssq_answer_matrix_voiceassist_20270804.pdf (answer matrix).

If it's helpful, we'd be happy to do a 30-minute walkthrough of the diagram and subprocessor mapping with your team later this week. Proposed times attached as a Calendly link in my signature.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

Thanks Stephanie — this is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our privacy team that we need in writing for the compliance pack: 

- Which subprocessors have staff or systems in the EU (we need a country-level breakdown)?
- For the PII scrubber: is it deterministic tokenization (reversible) or one-way pseudonymization by default? We need to know if transcripts can be re-identified and under what process.
- Can you provide an example of the audit export for transcript access requests (SAR) that our auditors could expect? Ideally a CSV sample with columns you would export (requester, file id, timestamp, action, redaction state).
- DPA clause: AcmeAssist requires that any subprocessor with access to raw audio be named in the DPA annex or be subject to a specific approval flow. Can you confirm Redwood's standard language for subprocessor addition and escalation?

Also, curious whether you have an HSM attestation/diagram we can include in our artifacts — particularly around BYO-KMS integrations for Dedicated.

If you can answer inline and add the sample audit CSV and subprocessor country mapping to the SSQ matrix, we'll sign off for the pilot review.

Best,
Elda

Hi Elda — following up with the additional artifacts you asked for. Quick answers inline, and attached the files: ssq_answer_matrix_voiceassist_20270804.pdf (updated with country mapping and sample audit CSV) and dpa_clause_suggestions_stephanie_20270804.txt. Highlights: 

- Subprocessor country mapping (summary): TranscodeCloud (US, DE), StorageTier (US, IE), MetricsStack (US), ThirdEye (US). Full org-level addresses included in the matrix.
- PII scrubber: default is one-way pseudonymization (non-reversible hashed token) when enabled; we offer reversible tokenization under contracted controls and with BYO-KMS for Private deployments. We call out reversible modes explicitly in the SSQ matrix.
- SAR/audit export sample: included in the matrix (sample CSV columns: request_id, requester_email, resource_id, action, timestamp_utc, retention_policy, redaction_state, processed_by).
- DPA subprocessor language: Redwood's standard is notification + 30-day approval window for named subprocessors; for AcmeAssist we can add an explicit approval gate for any new subprocessor that could access raw audio. Suggested clause text is in the attached TXT.
- HSM attestation: for Dedicated BYO-KMS we can provide HSM integration diagram and an HSM attestation template. Link to attestation (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-link-redwood/hsm-attestation (we will provide a signed attestation after contract).

Next steps proposal: 
1) We will add the per-country subprocessor addresses to the SSQ matrix and return the final PDF in 24 hours.
2) If you'd like the reversible tokenization option, we can prepare a focused ADDENDUM for the DPA that defines the controls and key handling requirements.
3) Book a 30-minute call so we can walk through the diagram and sign off on the pilot scope.

Would Thursday 8/5 11:00am ET or 3:00pm ET work for a walkthrough?
